chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi'l-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Surely, Allah the Majestic revealed to this world: 'Tire those who serve you and serve those who reject you.' If a servant were to seek his Master alone in the darkness of the night and whisper to Him, Allah would secure the light in his heart. If he were to say: 'O Lord! O Lord!', the Majestic would call to him: 'I am at your service, My servant. Ask Me and I will grant you. Rely on Me and I will suffice for you.'

Then He will say to His angels: 'O My angels! Look at My servant. He has sought Me alone in the darkness of the night while the idle ones are distracted and the heedless are asleep. Bear witness that I have forgiven him.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: Betake yourselves to piety, striving, and worship. Be ascetic in this world that is ascetic toward you, for surely it is deception — the abode of annihilation and evanescence. How many who were deceived by it were destroyed by it, how many who trusted it were betrayed by it, how many who relied on it were fooled and delivered to ruin. Know that before you is a dreadful path and a long journey. Your passage will be over the Bridge, and the traveler cannot do without provisions. Whoever journeys without preparing provisions will perish and be destroyed. The best provision is taqwa. Then remember your standing before Allah the Majestic, for He is the Just Judge. Prepare your answers to His questions, for He will surely ask you about how you treated the Two Weighty Things after me: the Book of Allah and my progeny.

Beware of saying: 'As for the Book, we changed it and interpolated it; and as for the progeny, we abandoned them and killed them.' At that point, your recompense will be nothing but the Fire. Whoever of you desires to be delivered from the terror of that Day should align with my wali and follow my deputy and my vicegerent after me, Ali ibn Abi Talib — for he is the master of my Pond. He will repel my enemies from it and water my friends from it. Whoever is not watered from it will forever be thirsty and never be quenched. Whoever drinks from it will never suffer hardship or thirst. Truly, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) is my standard-bearer in the Hereafter, just as he was my standard-bearer in this world. He will be the first to enter Paradise, because he will precede me with my standard in his hand, and beneath him will be Adam and those after him from the prophets.

key_terms.الثَّقَلَيْن: The Two Weighty Things — the Quran and the Prophet's progeny (Ahlulbayt), which the Prophet left as authoritative guides for the Muslim community
key_terms.الزَّاد: Provisions for the journey — metaphorically taqwa (God-consciousness) for the journey of the Hereafter
key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge — the path over hellfire that all must traverse on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.الْحَوْض: The Pond (Hawd al-Kawthar) — the eschatological pool from which the Prophet and Imam Ali will water the believers on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْوَرَع: Piety and scrupulousness — avoiding even doubtful matters

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the Two Weighty Things and the status of Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: This hadith is a prophetic sermon transmitted through the chain of the Imams from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW). It opens with a divine revelation about the nature of this world — that it exhausts those who pursue it and serves those who abandon it — then describes the profound reward of night devotion, before culminating in a passionate exhortation to asceticism, preparation for the Day of Judgment, adherence to the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, and the declaration of Ali ibn Abi Talib's supreme position as the Prophet's successor, standard-bearer, and guardian of the Pond.
